To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pigeons will peck for a secondary reinforcer and that the rate of pecking to obtain a secondary is equal to the rate of reinforcement by the primary.
the rate of responding in the presence of a stimulus that is correlated with the availability of primary reinforcers is a function of the relative rate of those primary reinforcers.

pigeons peck at a response-key at a rate proportional to the relative rate at which that key produces a primary reinforcer, and that this rate of primary reinforcement is proportional to the relative frequency with which the response-key is reinforced with a secondary reinforcer in the presence of a primary reinforcer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a particular type of secondary reinforcement, the secondary reinforcer that is a conditioned reinforcer.
the effect of the relative rate of reinforcement on behavior and the effect of behavior on relative rate of reinforcement.
the effects of secondary reinforcement on the behavior of pigeons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
secondary reinforcers are not substitutes for primary reinforcers.
the rate at which a pigeon pecks at the key that has produced a secondary rein- forceer is a function of the relative rate of the primary rein- forceer in the presence of that secondary reinforcer.
secondary reinforcement is a function of the relative rate at which the secondary reinforcer occurs in relation to the primary reinforcer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of primary reinforcement determines the relative rate at which the animal pecks for the secondary reinforcer.
the rate of pecking to obtain the primary reinforcer is a function of the rate at which the secondary reinforcer is obtained.
secondary reinforcement can be used to increase the rate of primary reinforcement.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the rate of primary reinforcement is the most important determinant of rate of secondary reinforcement, and the rate of secondary reinforcement is the main determinant of the rate of pecking in its presence.
the relative rate of reinforcement is an important variable in determining behavior.
secondary reinforcement can occur in the absence of a history of primary reinforcement.
